stmt: Every string that reaches a surface belongs to exactly one content entry and exactly one class. A string with no entry does not render. Improvised copy — a component composing text outside the registry — is a build failure, enforced by the same DOM-bound negative scan that already binds fixed strings.
Fixed entries render their text verbatim. The text is a contract; changing it is a contract-version change through the Rules Service ceremony at the ordinary tier.

Templated entries render only from named dependencies that resolve to verified fields. A Templated string contains no value that is not a dependency. The template is versioned; a version change is a ceremony.

Every Templated entry carries an honest-gap variant for each dependency that may be null. When a dependency is null, the variant renders. The template MUST NOT estimate, default, or infer a missing value.

Generated entries carry a class ceiling of inference or advisory and never fact. Every sentence in a Generated string anchors to material by provenance reference; an unanchored sentence is refused by Solva's existing floor before the gate, and the string passes A5.15 before display.

A number on any surface comes from a Templated dependency or a Fixed string. A Generated string MUST NOT introduce a number the surface does not already carry as a verified field. Prose may wrap a number; it never supplies one.
Which surfaces may carry Generated entries at all is a ruled list (R-32). A surface not on the list has no Generated entries, and a generation request from it is refused.

A content entry carries: entry identifier; surface; class; objective — one sentence stating what the string is for; template version or prompt version; dependencies, as named verified fields; honest-gap variants (Templated only); class ceiling and required anchors (Generated only); trigger; canon_ref where the string states or implies a governed fact; owner role.
A slot entry carries: slot identifier; surface; ordered candidate list; ranking rule version; hold rule (§5). A slot with an empty candidate list renders nothing.

The registry is read-only to every component except the ceremony engine. Templates, prompt versions, candidate lists, and ranking rule versions change only through ceremony. A model, a wizard, or a surface never writes an entry.

An objective is mandatory on every entry. An entry whose objective cannot be stated in one sentence is refused at ceremony — a string nobody can say the purpose of is a string nobody can say is still right.

Rendering is a pure function of (entry, entry version, dependency values). For Fixed and Templated entries it returns the string. For Generated entries it returns a generation request carrying the prompt version, the class ceiling, the required anchors, and the dependencies the prose may reference — and the drafting component's output re-enters the resolver for classing and gating before it becomes a string. No parameter exists through which a learned component's output can alter what a Fixed or Templated entry renders.

A learned component MAY propose a new template, a new candidate, or a re-ordering, through the research queue. The proposal is ratified by ceremony or it is nothing. Proposals never take effect on proposal.

The resolver fails closed. A missing dependency renders the honest-gap variant; a missing entry renders nothing; a Generated string that fails classing or the gate is refused with the platform's one refusal card. Nothing is improvised to fill a space.

Every candidate on a slot is assigned one salience class at render time, by the ranking rule, from its dependencies: Class 1 — a decision is required now (a job stopped at a limit, an approval pending on the reader, a ceiling or threshold crossed, a refusal the reader has not seen); Class 2 — something changed since the reader last saw this surface (a delta on a dependency, a status transition); Class 3 — an opportunity or capacity the reader can act on (room for more work, allowance available, resources idle); Class 4 — steady state (nothing pending, nothing changed, nothing to claim). The definitions are ruled (R-33) and versioned.

The hook is the eligible candidate with the lowest salience class. Ties resolve by the candidate list's order, which is fixed in the slot entry. The ranking is deterministic: the same dependency values produce the same hook.

An ineligible candidate — any dependency null — is never the hook while an eligible candidate exists in any class. If no candidate is eligible, the slot renders the honest-gap variant of the first-listed candidate. A gap is never headlined over a fact.

No engagement measure — views, dwell, clicks, replies — and no learned signal enters the ranking rule. The rule reads verified fields only. Salience is about what the reader must know to decide, not what the reader is likely to look at.

A hook holds until a candidate of a lower class becomes eligible or the hook's own dependencies change. A slot does not flap between candidates of equal class on unrelated updates. Hold values are ruled (R-34).

Choosing a hook writes a content receipt carrying the salience trace: every candidate, its class, its eligibility, and the rule version. The surface exposes the trace on demand — “why this first” — so a reader or overseer can see what the slot chose not to lead with.
A hook is advisory. It directs attention; it never gates an action, and a component MUST NOT treat the hook's class as an input to any decision the platform makes.

A chat answer, a recommendation body, or a notification body is a Generated entry on a surface R-32 permits. It passes Solva's classing, the A5.15 gate, and — where it recommends an action — carries A5.16 provenance. Within it, findings are ordered by the same salience classes as §5, applied by the resolver to the anchored findings before the drafting component composes prose around them. The model writes the sentences; it does not choose the order.

A displayed Generated string is stored as an artefact by hash with: class, anchors, prompt version, model identity and version (A5.7+, V-4), the content receipt. It is retrievable by hash for as long as the retention rule holds (R-35). A reader may see the anchors of any Generated string on demand.

A Generated string that would state a fact the anchors do not support is refused before display, not softened. Softening — hedging an unsupported claim into plausibility — is the slop this document exists to prevent, and A5.5 already forbids the silent downgrade it amounts to.

A Templated string is not stored as text. Its content receipt records template version and dependency values by reference; the string is re-derived on demand (CON-12). Storing the text would create a second copy that can disagree with its own inputs.
A Generated string is stored per CON-23. A Fixed string is stored once, as the contract. A hook choice is stored as its trace (CON-20).

Erasure reaches Generated artefacts. When a unit's rights are withdrawn, every Generated artefact whose anchors cite it is found by provenance and recalled or re-derived without it, on the mechanism DAP-38 and MEM-9 already define.
Retention of Generated artefacts follows a ruled default (R-35) and is subject to erasure precedence, on MEM-9's rule.

A Templated entry re-renders when any dependency changes. Dependency changes are the Ledger's own events — metered events, status transitions, receipts — so a surface is current to the record without a scheduler for any dependency that emits an event.
A schedule exists only for an entry with a dependency that emits no event. The schedule and its interval are recorded on the entry. A scheduled entry displays its as-of time.

If a trigger source is unreachable, the last rendered string displays with a visible stale marker and its as-of time. It is never silently held as current — the one degradation this platform permits, marked as the Browse census already is.
